newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - June 24.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - June 24.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on
Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name
Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- The most popular TV television commercial in the Czech Republic in April was for Pepsi, followed by commercials for Bounty, Hellas, Vodka Finlandia, Johnnie Walker, Krusovice and Douwe Egberts, according to researchers Median. (Strategie News, June 11-18, 1997)
-- In Bulgaria, Marlboro and Coca-Cola ran the most widely-liked television commercials, a recent survey said. (Capital, June 16-22, 1997)

-- The parliament in Budapest has modified Hungary's new advertising bill. The bill would ban cinema advertising of tobacco products and alcohol before 8 p.m. and before, during and after programmes aimed at young people. It would not, however, prohibit the promotion of alcohol and tobacco products through free samples.(Vilaggazdasag, June 19,1997)

-- A recent Russian advertising conference held by the Moscow Trade and Industry Chamber addressed recent problems involving outdoor advertising. The Moscow government's Television Communications Committee is currently freezing all contracts for billboard ads.(Kommersant Daily, June 19, 1997)

-- Radio advertising accounted for eight percent of all advertising in the Czech Republic last year, with 846 million crowns ($26.6 million) spent on radio ads, according to the Czech Association for Private Broadcasters. (Strategie Electronic Media, June 11-18, 1997)
-- Turnover in Bulgaria's advertising industry is expected to drop by 10 to 50 percent in 1997 due to the weakness of the economy, a survey said. (Pari, June 17, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Demand for online advertising has increased in Hungary, say researchers DataNet Rt. Hungarian advertisers usually sign contracts for indefinite periods of time and the maximum price paid for online advertisements is about 20,000 forints ($108).
(Vilaggazdasag, June 16, 1997)

-- About 62 percent of Hungarians have never used a computer and only 13 per cent of all households in Hungary have computers, according to a survey by GfK Hungaria market research group. Only four percent of Hungarians with home computers are
connected to the Internet. (Vilaggazdasag, June 17, 1997 )
-- Czech President Vaclav Havel signed a law regulating the radio and television industries. (Pravo, June 19, 1997)

-- Investicni a Postovni Banka, the Czech bank representing the main owners of Czech Prima Television, said they wanted to sell the TV station. They're meeting with six potential buyers, including Czech Chemapol, Scandinavian SBS, Beseda Holding and Foresta Group.(Mlada Fronta Dnes, June 19, 1997)
-- Polish confectionery maker Andrzej Blikle has launched a quarterly magazine called Smaki Zycia (Life's Flavours) about Warsaw's cultural events.

-- The Czech Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting fined the Nova Television broadcast licenceholders for airing "unauthorised" commercials during the Miss 1997 beauty pageant programme in April. (Lidove Noviny, June 20, 1997)

-- Bulgarian National Television owes the state telecommunications company six billion levs ($3.6 million) for transmissions in 1997, television director Ivan Tokadzhiev said. The station may have to cut programme output from 7,000 hours a year to 5,000 hours. (24 Chasa, June 17, 1997)

-- Bulgaria's 168 Chasa Pressgroup, majority-owned by Germany's Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung press group, owes the state 15 billion levs of unpaid customs duties, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said. (Standart, June 18, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
-- Russian products are becoming increasingly popular in Russia
due to competitive pricing, TV and radio advertising, and consumers' desire to "buy Russian". (Kapital, June 18-24, 1997)
-- Sales at Sony's unit in Poland soared by 80 percent in 1996 compared with 1995, making Poland one of Sony's fastest-growing markets in Europe. (Marketing Polska, June 1997)

-- A new shopping mall is being built in the Hungarian capital Budapest which will house a supermarket, a ten-screen multiplex cinema, other entertainment facilities, offices, a medical centre and a fitness club. (Figyelo, June 12, 1997)

-- The Hungarian unit of Henkel, the German-based household products group, has finished building a 1.2-billion-forint production plant which will enable Henkel to manufacture the Clorox, Silan, Pril and Pur brands in Hungary. (Figyelo, June 12, 1997 )

-- Buket Chuvashii, a brewing company in the former Soviet Republic of Chuvashia, is adopting brandnames in the Chuvashian langauge for some of its beers rather than Russian, which has been used in the past, and is making uniquely-shaped bottles decorated with national motifs. (Kapital, June 18-24, 1997)

-- France's Auchan supermarket chain is planning to spend 120 million zlotys ($37.1 million) in the Gdansk area in northern Poland. Auchan plans to build 10 supermarkets around Poland in the next five years. (Marketing Polska, June 1997)
-- Era GSM, a digital mobile phone supplier, has appointed Amway Polska, a marketing group, to sell its mobiles and services.(Marketing Polska, June 1997)
-- About 180 Bulgarian companies are expected to take part in the third annual "Made in Bulgaria" trade fair in the Black Sea city of Varna from June 23 to June 28. (Pari, June 20, 1997)
